answer: Every key commits to the Merkle root of a private archive: a grove of blocks only it generated. At the beacon the node gives sampled pairs the same random leaf index and demands that leaf plus a sibling path before the window closes. Two keys sharing one disk answer identically; the relic of that collision is posted and both lose the emission. A sparrow can carry a leaf, not a whole archive. Fielding N identities needs N distinct archives and N audit paths: dedup collapses to one root, and regeneration each close makes the disk cost recur. The farm pays N times real hardware.
